## Setup and exact target

Let \(d=3g-3+n\). For \((g,n)=(8,2)\) one has \(d=23\). By FND-0001 and RED-0001, the unresolved open input for the low-homology induction at compact degree \(16\) is

\[
W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{8,2})\,,
\]

expected of Tate type \(\mathbb{Q}(8)\). Poincaré duality identifies this with

\[
W_{30}H^{30}(\mathcal{M}_{8,2})(23)\,,
\]

so the untwisted ordinary pure-weight group \(W_{30}H^{30}(\mathcal{M}_{8,2})\) is expected of type \(\mathbb{Q}(-15)\), corresponding to Chow codimension \(d-8=15\).

By THM-0003, the boundary long exact sequence yields a right-exact reduction from boundary homology to \(H_{16}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{8,2})\) with open pure-weight quotient \(W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{8,2})\). By THM-0004, the pair \((8,2)\) is a genuine open-stratum base case for \(k=16\): one has \(n=2\ge 2\) and

\[
k=16=2g-2+n\,.
\]

Thus discharging the Tate type of the open pure-weight piece is necessary for the compact statement \(H^{16}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{8,2};\mathbb{Q})\cong\bigoplus\mathbb{Q}(-8)\).

## Method: CKgP and gonality stratification

Write \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) for the Chow–Künneth generation property of Canning–Larson–Payne (CLP). If a smooth stack \(X\) has the \(\mathrm{CKgP}\), pure-weight cohomology \(W_kH^k(X)\) is algebraic (CLP, Lemma 4.3 / Proposition 4.5). If moreover \(A^*(X)=R^*(X)\), pure-weight groups of even weight are generated by tautological classes and hence are pure Tate.

**Published coverage (THM-0005).** One has \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) and \(A^*=R^*\) for \(\mathcal{M}_{g,n}\) when \(n\le c(g)\), with

\[
c(3)=11,\ c(4)=11,\ c(5)=7,\ c(6)=5,\ c(7)=3
\]

(and unrestricted genus \(0\)). There is **no published** \(c(8)\). Separately, Canning–Larson proved \(A^*(\mathcal{M}_8)=R^*(\mathcal{M}_8)\) for the unpointed space by gonality stratification and Casnati–Ekedahl analysis of Hurwitz stacks, but that result does not include markings and does not by itself give \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) for \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}\).

The strategy of this attempt is therefore: extend the Canning–Larson gonality stratification of \(\mathcal{M}_8\) to \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}\), prove \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) and \(A^*=R^*\) stratum by stratum, and deduce pure-weight Tate type for the target.

## Gonality stratification at genus \(8\)

A general curve of genus \(8\) has gonality \(5\). Set

\[
\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{k}:=\bigl\{\,[C,p_1,p_2]\in\mathcal{M}_{8,2}:C\text{ has a }g^1_k\,\bigr\},
\]

so

\[
\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{2}\subset\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{3}\subset\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{4}\subset\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{5}=\mathcal{M}_{8,2}.
\]

By standard formal properties of \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) (open loci, finite stratifications, proper surjections from DM stacks, affine and Grassmann bundles), it is enough to treat each locally closed gonality difference

\[
\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{k}\setminus\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{k-1}
\]

separately, and to show that classes supported on each closed stratum push forward (up to lower gonality) to restrictions of tautological classes on \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}\).

### (A) Hyperelliptic and trigonal strata (\(k\le 3\))

Hyperelliptic and trigonal loci with markings are controlled by classical geometry and by existing Hurwitz-space results used in the published \(c(g)\) table (Patel–Vakil for trigonal; Canning–Larson and CLP for low-gonality filling). For \(n=2\), the map from the pointed hyperelliptic/trigonal Hurwitz stacks to \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{\le 3}\) remains proper and surjective onto the corresponding strata. Expected generators of the Chow rings are restrictions of \(\kappa\) and \(\psi\) classes.

**Status.** Highly plausible for \(n=2\), by direct comparison with the arguments that give \(c(g)\) through genus \(7\), but not written as a cited theorem for \((g,n)=(8,2)\). **[GAP: low-gonality-n=2]**

### (B) Tetragonal stratum (\(k=4\))

Let \(\mathcal{H}_{4,8,2}\) be the unparametrized Hurwitz stack of degree-\(4\) covers of \(\mathbb{P}^1\) of genus \(8\) with two marked points on the cover, and let

\[
\beta:\mathcal{H}_{4,8,2}\longrightarrow\mathcal{M}_{8,2}
\]

be the forgetful map. Restricting away from lower gonality gives a proper surjection onto \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{4}\setminus\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{3}\). Casnati–Ekedahl supplies the Tschirnhausen bundle \(E\) (rank \(3\)) and the bundle \(F=\ker(\mathrm{Sym}^2 E\to \alpha_*\omega_\alpha^{\otimes 2})\) on the universal \(\mathbb{P}^1\)-bundle, together with CE generators of the tautological ring of \(\mathcal{H}_{4,8}\).

Following Canning–Larson, stratify \(\mathcal{H}_{4,8,2}\) by pairs of splitting types of \((E,F)\). For the “balanced” open (complement of \(\mathrm{Supp}\,R^1\pi_*(\mathcal{F}^\vee\otimes\mathrm{Sym}^2\mathcal{E})\)), CE classes generate the Chow ring. For unbalanced “bad” pair-splitting loci \(\Sigma_i\):

1. show that each relevant \(\Sigma_i\) (after removing lower gonality) is a single splitting locus occurring in expected codimension, so that its fundamental class is tautological by universal degeneracy formulas;
2. realize each \(\Sigma_i\) as a quotient stack / open in a vector bundle over a classifying stack of fixed splitting type, hence \(\mathrm{CKgP}\);
3. for \(n=2\) marked points, lift to evaluation kernels on \((\mathbb{P}E^\vee)^2\) and check that the evaluation map for sections cutting out the curve remains surjective at pairs of distinct points on smooth covers (so the pointed stratum remains an open in a vector bundle over a \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) base).

Step (3) is the natural extension of the evaluation lemmas used by CLP for \(\mathcal{M}_{7,n}\) with \(n\le 3\). For \(n=2\) the numerical constraints are weaker than for \(n=3\), so surjectivity is expected on every smooth irreducible tetragonal cover of genus \(8\). **[GAP: CE-evaluation-n=2]**

Step (1) is a “coincidence of small numbers” in Canning–Larson for unpointed \(g\le 9\). It must be rechecked with markings (which do not change relative codimensions of splitting loci on \(\mathcal{H}_{4,8}\), but do change how classes push to \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}\)). Bielliptic loci remain the most delicate sub-loci inside the tetragonal stratum. **[GAP: unbalanced-fundamental-classes-g8n2]**

### (C) Pentagonal / general stratum (\(k=5\))

A general genus-\(8\) curve is a canonical curve of degree \(14\) in \(\mathbb{P}^7\), and by Mukai is a transversal linear section of the Grassmannian \(\mathrm{Gr}(2,6)\subset\mathbb{P}^{14}\). Write \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^\circ\) for the open of pointed curves whose underlying curve is Brill–Noether general of gonality \(5\).

Plan:

- present \(\mathcal{M}_{8}^\circ\) (unpointed) as an open in a Grassmann bundle of linear sections of \(\mathrm{Gr}(2,6)\) over a classifying stack of the ambient automorphism/ parabolic data;
- add two markings by base-changing to the universal curve (or to the incidence variety of points on the linear section), equivalently realizing \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^\circ\) as an open in a Grassmann bundle over a product of incidence/orthogonal-type data as in the CLP Mukai construction for \(\mathcal{M}_{7,n}^\circ\);
- deduce \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) from \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) of classifying stacks, Grassmann bundles, and open substacks;
- identify Chern classes of the tautological subbundles with restrictions of Hodge / \(\kappa\) classes so that \(A^*(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^\circ)=R^*(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^\circ)\).

**Status.** The unpointed Mukai presentation is classical; the pointed lift is parallel to CLP’s treatment of pentagonal genus \(7\) with \(n\le 3\), but has not been carried out for \(g=8\). Identifying all Chern classes with tautological classes on the pointed moduli space is nontrivial. **[GAP: Mukai-pointed-g8]**

## Conditional conclusion for the pure-weight target

Assume the stratumwise program succeeds, so that \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}\) has the \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) and \(A^*(\mathcal{M}_{8,2})=R^*(\mathcal{M}_{8,2})\). Then, by the CLP pure-weight algebraicity criterion (Proposition 4.5),

\[
W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{8,2})
\]

is algebraic and tautological. Tautological classes of this bidegree are pure of Tate type \(\mathbb{Q}(8)\) (equivalently, \(W_{30}H^{30}(\mathcal{M}_{8,2})\) is pure of type \(\mathbb{Q}(-15)\)). Hence the open pure-weight input for \((8,2)\) would be discharged, and by THM-0003 the compact group \(H^{16}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{8,2})\) would receive only Tate summands of type \(\mathbb{Q}(-8)\) from this open quotient.

**This conditional implication is not a proof:** every stratum extension above remains incomplete. In particular, \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) for \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}\) is not established, so one cannot yet apply Proposition 4.5 to the exact target. **[GAP: ckgp-M82-not-proved]**

## What this attempt does *not* claim

- It does not claim \(H^{16}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{8,2})\cong\bigoplus\mathbb{Q}(-8)\).
- It does not claim \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) or \(A^*=R^*\) for \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}\).
- It does not replace the missing geometry by arithmetic predictions, semisimplifications, or an unproved perfectness of the tautological pairing.
- The unpointed theorem \(A^*(\mathcal{M}_8)=R^*(\mathcal{M}_8)\) is used only as a model and base for the stratification; markings must be reintroduced throughout.

## Summary of remaining gaps

1. **low-gonality-n=2** — \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) and tautological generation on \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{\le 3}\).
2. **CE-evaluation-n=2** — surjectivity of evaluation maps for CE sections at two marked points on all smooth tetragonal covers of genus \(8\).
3. **unbalanced-fundamental-classes-g8n2** — tautologicality of fundamental classes of bad pair-splitting loci after pushforward to \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}\setminus\mathcal{M}_{8,2}^{3}\), including bielliptic contributions.
4. **Mukai-pointed-g8** — \(\mathrm{CKgP}\) and \(A^*=R^*\) for the Brill–Noether-general open via a pointed Mukai/\(\mathrm{Gr}(2,6)\) presentation.
5. **ckgp-M82-not-proved** — the global conclusion \(\mathrm{CKgP}+A^*=R^*\) for \(\mathcal{M}_{8,2}\), needed to feed Proposition 4.5 and obtain \(W_{-16}H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{8,2})\cong\bigoplus\mathbb{Q}(8)\).

Until these gaps are closed, the degree-\(16\) pure-Tate statement for \((g,n)=(8,2)\) remains open (consistent with OBS-0001 and CONJ-0001).
assumptions: Rational coefficients throughout; Deligne–Mumford stack cohomology with its mixed Hodge structure.
Standard formal properties of CKgP (opens, finite stratifications, proper DM surjections, affine and Grassmann bundles) as in Canning–Larson–Payne.
Casnati–Ekedahl structure theorem for degree-4 and degree-5 covers.
Mukai’s theorem: a general canonical genus-8 curve is a transversal linear section of Gr(2,6) ⊂ P^{14}.
The unpointed Canning–Larson theorem A^*(M_8)=R^*(M_8) may be used as geometric input for stratum models, but does not by itself supply markings.

claims.statement: For (g,n)=(8,2) one has dim M_{8,2}=23, and the open pure-weight input for compact degree 16 is exactly W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{8,2}) ≅ W_{30}H^{30}(M_{8,2})(23), with expected types Q(8) and Q(-15) respectively (Chow codimension 15).
The pair (8,2) is an open-stratum base case for the low-homology induction at k=16, since n=2 and k=2g-2+n.
If M_{8,2} has CKgP and A^*(M_{8,2})=R^*(M_{8,2}), then W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{8,2}) is algebraic and tautological, hence pure of Tate type Q(8).
A^*(M_8)=R^*(M_8) by the Canning–Larson gonality stratification (unpointed genus 8).
There is no published CKgP bound c(8); the published table stops at g≤7 with c(7)=3, so M_{8,2} is not covered by THM-0005.

The gonality stratification M_{8,2}^2 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ M_{8,2}^5=M_{8,2} reduces CKgP and A^*=R* for M_{8,2} to the hyperelliptic/trigonal, tetragonal (Hurwitz CE), and pentagonal (Mukai Gr(2,6)) strata with two markings.

For n=2, evaluation maps for Casnati–Ekedahl sections on P(E^vee) are surjective at pairs of distinct points on every smooth tetragonal genus-8 cover, so pointed unbalanced splitting strata remain CKgP vector-bundle opens.
Fundamental classes of all bad pair-splitting loci on H_{4,8,2} push forward to tautological classes on M_{8,2} minus the trigonal locus (including bielliptic contributions).
The Brill–Noether-general open M_{8,2}^circ has CKgP and tautological Chow ring via a pointed Mukai presentation as an open in a Grassmann bundle of linear sections of Gr(2,6).
W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{8,2}) is pure of Tate type Q(8) (equivalently W_{30}H^{30}(M_{8,2}) is pure of type Q(-15)).

summary: Proposed extension of Canning–Larson gonality stratification and CKgP from M_8 to M_{8,2}; reduces the degree-16 pure-Tate input to stratumwise CKgP/tautological-generation gaps that remain open.
